newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Petroleum Refinery 1996 profits up.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Petroleum Refinery 1996 profits up.

text.p: Jordan Petroleum Refinery Company's 1996 net profits rose five percent to 6.8 million dinars ($9.6 million), its annual report showed.

Its pre-tax profits for 1996 dropped to 8.5 million dinars against 11.4 million dinars in 1995, the firm's balance sheet showed. But a sharp cut in corporate tax last year helped to raise its net profits.
The company blames the government for strangling its profits by an accord which sets a rigid pricing formula for its purchases of imported Iraqi crude, not linked to market prices.
It wants the government to abolish the concession and to operate commercially.
The company was supplied by Iraq with 3,274,296 tonnes of crude oil in 1996, a three percent rise from the previous year.
Its refined products imports, also mainly from Iraq, rose a steep 28.6 percent in 1996 to 1,192,207 tonnes.
Iraq alone supplied 52,599 tonnes of liquid gas, 19,856 tonnes of gasoline, 809,301 tonnes of fuel oil, and 278,071 tonnes of heating fuel.
Smaller quantities of refined products were also imported from Lebanon, Turkey and from Greece by vessels.
The company's only refinery located in Zarqa processed 3,253,948 tonnes of crude oil in 1996 which produced 3,154,247 tonnes of products for the domestic market, a two percent increase from 1995.
Its sales of various petroleum products totalled 4,136,155 tonnes in 1996, a nearly four percent increase from the previous year.
Jordan Petroleum Company is currently undertaking 33.3 million dinars worth of projects to modernise its facilities, including a 16.7 million dinars storage tank project in Aqaba.
